title: session-affinity-and-snapshotting-notes
content:
Context / goal:

This is a personal sketch for how we might implement lightweight session affinity + periodic snapshotting of session state (KV / prefix cache / model KV cache references) on the inference runtime. The intent: allow client libraries to reconnect to other nodes without losing KV context for active sessions while keeping memory use bounded and preserving latency SLOs.

Primary constraints:
- Minimal tail-latency impact on token generation path (no sync disk writes on hot path).
- Snapshot data should be small (references to KV pages + checkpointed prefix tokens), ideally incremental diffs.
- No strong cross-node coordination (we prefer eventual consistency + TTL-based invalidation).
- Support private deployments (no reliance on cloud services by default).
- Must be compatible with current batching and KV cache eviction heuristics.

Assumed primitives we already have:
- In-memory session object: session_id -> {kv_refs: list, prefix_hash, last_active_ts, owner_worker_id} (kept in runtime process memory)
- Background threads and disk area accessible to runtime (local FS or mounted volume in Private deployments)
- Small metadata store (BoltDB / RocksDB) available for indexing snapshots on Dedicated/Private

High-level approach (sketch):
1) Session affinity token: client keeps a short-lived affinity token (AFF-T) that encodes preferred worker id + version + signature. AFF-T is returned on session creation and rotated on reconnects.
2) Periodic snapshotting: owning worker writes incremental snapshot blobs to local storage or a configured shared store every N seconds or after X tokens. Snapshot metadata written to local index DB.
3) Reconnect flow: client presents session_id + AFF-T. If connecting to same worker and live, continue. Else, the target worker looks up latest snapshot and applies it in-memory before resuming generation. If no snapshot or stale, fallback to re-generation.

API shapes (HTTP/SDK):
- POST /v1/sessions (create) -> {session_id, affinity_token, owner_worker_id, snapshot_interval_seconds}
- POST /v1/sessions/{id}/snapshot (internal) -> {snapshot_id, base_seq, delta_size_bytes}
- GET  /v1/sessions/{id}/snapshot/latest -> {snapshot_id, available_at, snapshot_url?}
- POST /v1/sessions/{id}/reconnect -> {provided_affinity_token, expected_worker_id?} returns {reconnect_status: ok|migrate|stale, apply_steps: [...], new_affinity_token}

Notes on tokens: affinity_token structure (compact): base64( worker_id || version || expiry_ts || hmac ). HMAC uses runtime key derived from node identity. Short TTL (e.g., 30m) to keep stale routing limited.

Snapshot content considerations:
- We store: minimal list of KV chunk ids (opaque ids), a compact serialized prefix (first K tokens since session start or since last snapshot), and small metadata (seq numbers, model hash, quantization profile id).
- The actual KV binary payloads are stored as chunked objects on disk keyed by chunk id. Chunks can be deduplicated across sessions if same page content.
- Snapshots are write-once append blobs. Older snapshots garbage-collected after TTL or when session idle-longer-than threshold.

In-memory layout (ASCII):

[worker process memory]
|-- sessions_map (map)
|    |-- session_abc123 -> {owner_worker: w-17, last_active: 2026-02-01T11:33Z, prefix_hash: h1, kv_refs: [c1,c7], seq: 412}
|    |-- session_def456 -> {...}

[local store / snapshots dir]
/var/lib/redwood/snapshots/<worker_id>/<session_id>/<snapshot_id>.blob   (binary chunks + small json meta)
/var/lib/redwood/index.db  -- key: session_id -> latest_snapshot_id, last_touch_ts

Reconnect flow (detailed):
1) client opens connection to runtime node X with session_id S and AFF-T token.
2) Node X checks if it is owner_worker for S. If yes and session present -> attach immediately.
3) If not owner OR owner absent -> node X consults local index.db (if shared store configured, check remote index store). If latest snapshot found:
   a) stream snapshot blob(s) and rehydrate minimal prefix + register kv_refs in mem map.
   b) validate model_hash and quant profile; if mismatch -> reply migrate|stale.
4) If no snapshot found -> reply reconnect_status: stale (client must re-run from scratch).

Failure modes and heuristics:
- Owner worker crashed immediately after writing snapshot meta but before flush of chunks -> mark snapshot as "maybe incomplete". We can detect via snapshot metadata checksums; if incomplete, ignore and try previous snapshot.
- Snapshot write latency spikes during GC -> background writer should back off; if backlog grows > threshold, increase interval or switch to event-based (write after N tokens only).
- Disk full -> stop snapshotting new sessions; mark sessions as non-migratable (affinity enforced) and surfacing to metrics/alerts.

Rollout / migration plan (canary):
- Phase 0: Internal runtime tests + synthetic client that rapidly creates 10k sessions and reconnects randomly. Verify memory usage and snapshot write throughput.
- Phase 1: Enable for dev/staging clusters. Expose metrics: snapshot_write_latency, snapshot_size_bytes, reconnect_success_rate, average_rehydrate_time.
- Phase 2: Beta flag for 10% of hosted traffic (non-sensitive). Monitor errors, fallback rate, and tail latency.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How big should prefix snapshots be? Tradeoff between rehydrate time and snapshot size. Proposal: default to 512 tokens, configurable per-client.
- Dedup across workers: do we want a shared object store for chunk dedupe in Dedicated deployments? Pros: less storage. Cons: adds network dependency. Leave optional.
- Security: AFF-T HMAC key rotation across nodes. Need KMS integration for Private (bring-your-own-key).
- Garbage collection policy: session idle TTL vs per-customer retention policy.
- Metrics to add to tracing: time_to_first_token_after_reconnect, snapshot_apply_time percentile.

Experiment ideas (quick):
- Compare two snapshot policies: periodic (every 30s) vs delta-on-commit (after N tokens). Measure cost and reconnect time.
- Try a tiny prioritized snapshot: always include the last M tokens used by the shortest-latency paths (e.g., tool-calls) and skip larger context until on-demand pull.

Small checklist before next sync with Priya/Ethan:
- [ ] Draft internal API for snapshot blob format (proto or compact msgpack)
- [ ] Add index DB schema notes (keys + TTL semantics)
- [ ] Build small PoC that runs in local dev cluster using FS-backed snapshots (no external object store)
- [ ] Add metrics instrumentation hooks to snapshot writer and rehydration path
- [ ] Write brief confluence note and link to GH PR template

Rough timeline (personal estimate):
- PoC + microbench: 3 weeks
- Internal test+fixes: 2 weeks
- Staged rollout + monitoring tweaks: 4 weeks

Notes-to-self: keep snapshots small and biased toward fast rehydrate. When in doubt prefer falling back to stateless reconnect over heavy synchronous writes.

References / related tickets:
- INF-612 (session-migration edge cases)
- PR #4410 (kv-chunk-dedupe)
- Slack thread: #runtime-session-handles (Jan 2026)

---
Small off-topic idea: consider a light-weight "session sidecar" that holds snapshots for a group of workers as a local clustered service (raft-lite) — cheaper than full object-store and faster than remote S3. Worth a spike later.

End of scratchpad.
